section_summary: This section contains State Department and USPOLAD Tokyo reporting from late December 1949 on economic affairs in occupied Japan and the Ryukyu Islands. Documents include biweekly Washington progress summaries and Tokyo airgrams covering government employee wage disputes and year-end bonuses, foreign trade arrangements with Burma, Thailand, Sweden, and the sterling area, precious metals disposal, and private import regulations. The section concludes with USPOLAD Despatch No. 911 transmitting a comprehensive 14-page SCAP mission report on Ryukyuan economic stabilization, proposing new foreign exchange rates, wage scales, and counterpart funding procedures.

subfiles.about: Summarizes policy developments concerning Korean maritime claims, FEC reparations, petroleum imports, an IBRD mission, ship repairs, Far East economic reporting, and Ryukyuan administration.
subfiles.from: Noel Hemmendinger and C. T. White, Office of Northeast Asian Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Reports on Korean vessel restitution claims, FEC industrial level decisions, sterling oil imports, an IBRD Far East mission, repair of the S.S. Conte Verde, an economic reporting conference, and a proposed directive for the Ryukyus.
subfiles.title: Biweekly Summary of Economic Developments: Japan and the Ryukyus

subfiles.about: Transmits intelligence on Japanese government year-end bonuses, looted gold disposal, ESS personnel actions, overseas trade offices, import regulations, and reparations committee dissolution.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports on government year-end bonus authorization, proposed liquidation of looted precious metals, Halff's suspension, SCAP's New York shipping office, private import regulations, dollar store restrictions, Burmese rice offers, and RTAC dissolution.
subfiles.title: USPOLAD Tokyo Airgram A-387 on Economic Developments in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits intelligence on the postponement of the Japanese budget, the Anglo-American textile mission, wool glove exports, trade agreements, and maritime law protests.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports on withholding the fiscal 1950-51 national budget, conditions for the Anglo-American textile mission, knit wool glove exports to the U.S., the Thailand trade plan, British and Danish shipping protests, and open-account trade audits.
subfiles.title: USPOLAD Tokyo Airgram A-399 on Economic Developments in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits a copy of the SCAP mission report on Okinawa regarding exchange rates, wages, and economic procedures.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, Acting Political Adviser, Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits the report of the SCAP mission to Okinawa pursuant to Department airgram instruction no. 239.
subfiles.title: USPOLAD Tokyo Despatch No. 911: Transmission of Report of SCAP Mission to Okinawa

subfiles.about: Presents findings and policy recommendations on foreign exchange rates, wage levels, imported commodity pricing, and financial procedures in the Ryukyu Islands.
subfiles.summary: Recommends establishing an internal and commercial exchange rate of 120-to-1 (Ryukyuan yen to U.S. dollar) and a 50-to-1 conversion ratio for pricing GARIOA imports. Proposes establishing a minimum monthly wage of approximately 2,000 yen for military workers, eliminating subsidized compound meals and trade stores, and aligning civilian administration wages. Urges expanding consumer goods imports from Japan to curb inflation during the U.S. military construction program, coordinating the Ryukyu Military Government budget with the U.S. fiscal year, and providing counterpart rehabilitation loans through the Bank of the Ryukyus.
subfiles.title: Report of SCAP Mission to Okinawa
